findings.title: Bootstrap envelope trust fails open: stripping the signature field yields a fully 'trusted' envelope with exit 0
findings.explanation: The entire keyring/expiry/audience/fingerprint machinery is conditional on the attacker-controlled presence of a signature field: an envelope tampered in transit or on disk can delete the field and validateEnvelope returns {trusted:true} with verify exiting 0, only the secondary signed:false flag distinguishing it. The no-signature flow is a documented, test-pinned interim state (bootstrap-trust.test.mjs asserts a signature-stripped envelope passes with ok:true), the embedded keyring is self-labeled test-fixture-only, and docs/production-readiness-report.md tracks production signatures as gate G2 — but the publication gate is process/comment, not code, and an exit-code-only consumer cannot distinguish unsigned-ok from signed-ok.
findings.impact: Any party able to modify the envelope or package distribution — the exact threat the envelope exists for — bypasses all crypto controls by removing one JSON field; consumers checking only verification.ok accept the tampered payload.
findings.remediationSketch: Default to rejecting unsigned envelopes (or gate acceptance on a persisted out-of-band TOFU acknowledgment); make verify exit non-zero for unsigned envelopes unless --allow-unsigned is passed; require signature before any payload-write path in the consuming engine.

challenges.rationale: Mechanics accurate but this is a documented, test-pinned interim posture (publication-gated comment, explicit bootstrap-trust tests, fixture-only keyring, readiness-report G2); residual risk is that nothing mechanically fails closed at publication time — medium, not high.

findings.title: Host default Node v20.20.2 is past EOL; repo tooling mitigates but bare `node` invocations still hit it
findings.explanation: The repo pins 22.23.2 (current, supported to 2027-04-30), CI uses setup-node from .node-version, and with-node22 re-execs under v22-v24; engines is advisory, so bare `node` runs the EOL host default and per F-024 can silently no-op rather than fail.
findings.impact: Developer-ergonomics residual on the EOL host runtime.
findings.remediationSketch: Optionally set engine-strict or have entry scripts assert the Node major with a clear error.

findings.title: CDP auth token rides in the URL query string of every consumer URL
findings.explanation: The token is embedded as ?token= in three persisted URL copies; every observed sink redacts consistently and files are 0600, so safety depends on each future call site remembering redaction rather than a structural property.
findings.impact: Any newly added unredacted logger of cdpUrl/wsUrl would leak a live loopback token (cheap rotation mitigates).
findings.remediationSketch: Add a check-skill rule flagging unredacted interpolation of the raw endpoint fields.
